_comment: PYNQ-Z1 Rocket SoC, 40.000 MHz.  PERIODIC arm: SignDetLite is the REAL-TIME PERIODIC task at period 1000 ms (1.00 fps) and Moonshine is the NON-PERIODIC job being measured around it.  Costs are board-measured per dispatch and are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the non-periodic spec's -- the profile CSVs, dispatch graphs and contention artifacts are the same files.  SignDetLite's costs: out/b145_signdet_f167/run.json, Lab B145, 0x5A5A0038 md5 ced0aab0c7b52f25338eeffe8f678e4f, FCLK0 40.000 MHz, gate.max_abs_err 0 -- 8 dispatches, 9,514,643 measured cycles.  CROSS-BITSTREAM NOTE, stated because it is load-bearing: Moonshine's per-dispatch costs were measured on 0x5A5A0035 and SignDetLite's on 0x5A5A0038.  Both are 40.000 MHz, both carry the same md5-pinned nch=8 RoccMoon engine snapshot (src/lanes_engine_b98nch8b/) on hart 1 and the same MBP P-extension on hart 0, and RocketALU.sv / RoccMoonEngine.sv / RoccMoonShim.sv are byte-identical between the two elaborations; 0x5A5A0038 reproduced B134's nine board tokens at +0.033 % of 0x5A5A0035's cycle count (MAGIC_REGISTRY.md, 0x5A5A0038).  The co-location itself needs the engine, so it targets 0x5A5A0038 -- 0x5A5A0039 has TACIT and NO engine, which is where SignDetLite could run but Moonshine could not.
_basis_warning: THE MAKESPAN IN THIS ARM IS NOT THE MAKESPAN IN THE NON-PERIODIC ARM.  restrict_makespan_to_nonperiodic is TRUE here, so the reported figure is MOONSHINE'S COMPLETION ALONE, measured around the detector's reserved instances; the detector's own tail is excluded from it (run_xpurt_schedule.py:1069).  In networks_pynqz1_coloc2m_sd_<arm>.json the flag is FALSE and the figure is the max over both networks.  The two tables are on different bases and must not be differenced.  op_deadline_miss_count also changes meaning: Moonshine carries no max_end_t here, so only late DETECTOR dispatches are counted.
_machines_comment: TWO MACHINES, each holding an opcode the other traps on.  CPU_P is hart 0 (MBP P-extension, custom-0); CPU_E is hart 1 (RoccMoon engine and lanes, custom-1).  Unchanged from the non-periodic spec.
_periodic_comment: num_instances is DECLARED, not left to workload_factory._estimate_num_periodic_instances.  That heuristic sizes the horizon from the sum over non-periodic dispatches of the WORST machine's cost, and Moonshine's worst machine is the EXCLUDED one, whose cost is profile_loader._penalise_unsupported's capped penalty -- 228,733 ms (b1) / 222,131 ms (b4) of pure exclusion artifact, which at T = 250 ms would ask for 915 detector instances.  Declared here as ceil(4000 / 1000) = 4: the detector firing continuously through ONE 4.0 s utterance window.  horizon_ms is the same 4000 ms so prune_periodic's trim cuts at max(4000, moonshine_makespan) and deletes nothing the demo would run.
_what_is_NOT_modelled: THE SCHEDULE HOLDS THE 8 MODEL DISPATCHES ONLY.  B146 measured the real demo frame end to end at ~550 ms on silicon: inference 237.8 + front end 80.9 + L2 sweep 68.6 + OLED 86.1 + capture ~70.  The front end, the sweep, the OLED write and the capture are NOT in this graph, so a period of 550 ms here understates the true hart-0 load by roughly 2x.  A crossing point read off this table is 'the scheduler says it fits', not 'the board can do it'.
_cells_comment: CROSS TERMS ARE NOT FABRICATED -- identical to the non-periodic spec.  Three classes: measured; excluded_impossible (illegal instruction there, no alternative body); excluded_unmeasured (a runnable body exists, nothing in this tree has timed it).  SignDetLite contributes ZERO excluded_unmeasured cells; all its CPU_E cells are impossible.

_definition.measured: a board run in this tree executed this dispatch on this machine and recorded cycles
_definition.excluded_impossible: the selected kernel's executed body traps on an absent opcode there, and the kernel holds no body that machine could execute
_definition.excluded_unmeasured: a body that machine could execute exists in the same kernel, but nothing in this tree has measured it

_contention_comment: Same artifacts as the non-periodic solve, unchanged.  contention_model.canonical_key strips the periodic instance index (signdet3_dispatch_5 -> signdet:5), so one per-dispatch table covers every instance -- contention is a property of the kernel, not of which instance is running it.  DRAM plateau aggregate 0.924 (headline); L2 edge 0.549 (sensitivity, the single worst point on the curve).

moonshine._note: NON-PERIODIC: no period, no window_duration, so this is the job the makespan measures.  12 decoder steps, 2253 dispatches, 3532.6 ms if serialised.  Its real-time requirement is the 4000 ms utterance window, tested against the reported makespan rather than by a max_end_t.
moonshine._split: 751 dispatches on CPU_E (hart 1) and 1502 on CPU_P (hart 0)

signdet._note: PERIODIC at 1000 ms (1.00 fps), 4 instances x 8 dispatches = 32 ops.  Instance i occupies [i*1000, (i+1)*1000] ms.  Each instance is 237.87 ms of measured hart-0 work, so the model-dispatch duty cycle alone is 23.8 % of one hart -- before the front end, L2 sweep, OLED and capture that _what_is_NOT_modelled names.
signdet._split: all on CPU_P (hart 0) -- STRUCTURAL truth, not a runtime outcome: no engine kernel exists for conv2d_s8_pc / permute4_s8 / softmax_s8 at all, so the engine runtime is never linked.  B145 measured engine.runtime_linked=false and mbxr_rt_stats absent from the ELF.  SignDetLite is PINNED to CPU_P, not scheduled there.

_arm_note: b4 (--batch-decode): encoder dispatches scaled by the measured x0.9932 back-to-back factor and decoder dispatches by the measured x0.5883 batch-4 factor (B129).  Region factors applied uniformly inside a region is the model.  The DETECTOR is never scaled: it is not batched.
